findings.summary: The site is fixed to a light theme.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme, light-dark(), or color-scheme adaptation; the dark-emulated screenshot remains the same light Cookiebot surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark tokens for page and consent surfaces.

findings.summary: Motion continues when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the active-animation probe returned at least 100 running animations, including 1.37s to 67s durations; CSS inspection found no reduced-motion media rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce layer that removes non-essential transitions, marquee/auto-advance motion, and long-running effects.

findings.summary: The UI does not explicitly adapt to increased contrast or forced colors.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors handling; Lighthouse also found four concrete color-contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast treatments for controls, links, focus indicators, and custom scroll/UI chrome.

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation swaps abruptly.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across the MPA found no view-transition rules, while the representative paths are ordinary same-origin document navigations.
findings.suggestedFix: Use @view-transition { navigation: auto } and stable view-transition-name values for shared page chrome, with reduced-motion safeguards.

findings.summary: Long news pages offer no scroll-state-aware orientation aid.
findings.evidence: The article is a long page and CSS inspection found no scroll-state query or scroll progress mechanism; captured first viewport has navigation but no reading progress cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight declarative reading-progress indicator or scroll-state-aware compact header.

findings.summary: A consent wall obscures all content on every fresh visit.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile load screenshots show a viewport-dominating Cookiebot dialog before any interaction; on mobile the content is almost entirely unavailable behind it.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the first-layer copy and footprint while retaining equally prominent accept and necessary-only choices; keep essential content legible around the consent UI where legally permissible.

findings.summary: The blocking consent modal is implemented as custom ARIA dialog chrome rather than a native dialog.
findings.evidence: DOM probe found role=dialog but zero <dialog> elements, popovers, or details; the overlay relies on custom behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog for the blocking consent flow, with focus restoration and platform dismissal behavior appropriate to consent requirements.

findings.summary: Several controls are too small or too tightly spaced for touch.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse target-size failed with six items, and the DOM geometry probe found 25 of 145 visible interactive elements below 44px in at least one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase control hit areas and spacing to at least 44 CSS px where practical, without enlarging visual glyphs unnecessarily.

findings.summary: The mobile load is very slow.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 12.8s, FCP 4.0s, TBT 1,471ms, and performance score 34; the independent trace still measured LCP 2.65s and TBT 673ms under a lighter run.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP element, prioritize its request, remove critical-chain delays, and defer non-essential JavaScript and ad/consent integrations.

findings.summary: Long main-thread tasks delay responsiveness.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded three long tasks, including a 564ms task, and 673ms TBT; Lighthouse measured 1,471ms TBT and 1,040ms max potential input delay.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up long tasks, yield between work chunks, and delay third-party initialization until it is needed or consented.

findings.summary: The initial network payload is script-heavy.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 68 requests and 2,036,416 transferred bytes; 33 scripts accounted for 1,539,977 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit critical scripts, use defer/module semantics, prioritize only LCP-critical resources, and lazy-load consented ad/analytics code.

findings.summary: Third-party and application JavaScript dominate the page weight.
findings.evidence: Scripts are 76% of the 2.04MB transfer in the HAR, before the user has made a consent choice, and 18 third-party origins are contacted.
findings.suggestedFix: Use coverage/bundle analysis to remove unused code and gate optional vendor bundles behind interaction and consent.

findings.summary: Some text does not meet minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast audit failed four elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to meet WCAG AA, then verify normal, hover, disabled, and consent states.

findings.summary: Document structure is weaker than the visual navigation suggests.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flagged heading order, while the DOM probe found a main and footer but no semantic nav or header landmarks on a page with extensive navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use header/nav landmarks and repair heading hierarchy without changing the visual layout.

findings.summary: Touch target sizing fails the inclusive reflow/input bar.
findings.evidence: The 360px layouts do not overflow, but Lighthouse target-size failed six items and the probe found 25 controls below 44px.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target hit areas and re-test at narrow viewport and 200% zoom.

findings.summary: The page logs runtime and network errors on load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a CORS failure for aid.no plus failed 400 and 401 authentication requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Prevent unauthenticated identity calls from failing noisily and fix the aid.no CORS contract or avoid the request until needed.

findings.summary: The page is not eligible for BFCache and reports browser inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the BFCache audit and reported an Issues-panel item, alongside a third-party-cookie warning.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unload/cache blockers and resolve the reported browser issue; verify back/forward restoration in DevTools.

findings.summary: The CSP is too weak to mitigate script injection and HSTS is absent.
findings.evidence: Headers show HTTPS and nosniff, but CSP contains only upgrade-insecure-requests and HSTS is missing.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforcing nonce/hash-based CSP and HSTS after validating all subdomains.

findings.summary: The pre-consent third-party footprint is broad.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe saw 18 third-party origins and known Google Tag Manager/DoubleClick endpoints before consent; the HAR captured 2.04MB and the UI discloses 1,022 potential partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors, prevent non-essential endpoints from loading before consent, and batch only necessary analytics after consent.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced policies are missing.
findings.evidence: Headers lack HSTS, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy; CSP does not define frame-ancestors or script restrictions, though X-Frame-Options is SAMEORIGIN.
findings.suggestedFix: Add strict Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, move clickjacking defense into CSP frame-ancestors, and harden CSP.

findings.summary: The tip form omits useful autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: The form probe found empty autocomplete attributes for email and telephone fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Add email and tel autocomplete tokens so returning tipsters can use browser autofill.

findings.summary: Substantial script and vendor work runs before user intent is known.
findings.evidence: The initial HAR transfers 1.54MB of script and contacts 18 third-party origins; trace TBT is 673ms before consent interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer and deprioritize background/vendor fetching until consent or a feature interaction makes it necessary.

findings.summary: Third-party cost is disproportionate for a text-led news landing page.
findings.evidence: Eighteen third-party origins contribute to a 2.04MB initial transfer, with 33 scripts and known advertising/tracking endpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party request/byte budget, remove low-value vendors, and load remaining integrations on demand.

findings.summary: The site deliberately blocks GPTBot and exposes no structured agent capability.
findings.evidence: robots.txt contains User-agent: GPTBot followed by Disallow: /; the DOM probe found no WebMCP surface. Search crawling remains available and article HTML is server-rendered.
findings.suggestedFix: If agent reach is a product goal, define an explicit AI crawler policy and expose safe read/search capabilities in structured form; otherwise document the deliberate opt-out.

findings.summary: Retained heap grew after repeated menu interaction.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary was 56,012,069 bytes/847,335 nodes; after ten menu open/close cycles it was 63,030,449 bytes/958,461 nodes, about 12.5% more bytes and 13.1% more nodes. Separate fresh browser sessions make this a medium-confidence leak signal, not proof of a specific retained path.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat in one instrumented session with baseline/target/final snapshots, then remove retained menu nodes, listeners, observers, or caches identified by the comparison.

findings.summary: The initial memory and DOM footprint is high for a news landing page.
findings.evidence: A fresh-load heap summary contains 847,335 nodes and 56.0MB self size, including 308,677 native nodes and 34,756 closures.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce initially rendered consent/vendor DOM, virtualize or defer below-fold content, and unload optional integrations.

taskList.title: Cut critical-path JavaScript and repair LCP/main-thread performance
Reduce and gate the pre-consent third-party footprint
Shrink the consent wall and use a robust modal primitive
Harden CSP, HSTS, and browser security policies
Respect dark, reduced-motion, and contrast preferences
Repair contrast, landmarks, and target sizing
Investigate memory growth and reduce initial footprint
Clean up console, BFCache, and inspector failures
Add autofill assistance to the tip form
Define an explicit agent/crawler capability policy
